scenes.title: A Moving Object on a Surface
scenes.narration: Imagine kicking a football or pushing a heavy wooden crate across a surface. An applied force sets the object into forward motion with velocity v.
scenes.onScreenText:
1. Motion and Applied Force
Object moving across surface with Velocity (v →)
scenes.subtitles: An applied force sets an object into forward motion across a surface with velocity v.

scenes.title: The Surfaces in Contact
scenes.narration: Even surfaces that feel smooth to our touch are covered with countless microscopic hills, valleys, and irregularities when viewed closely.
scenes.onScreenText:
2. Microscopic Contact Nature
Solid surfaces have microscopic hills & valleys
scenes.subtitles: Even smooth surfaces have countless microscopic hills and valleys when viewed under magnification.

scenes.title: Friction Force Appears
scenes.narration: As the surfaces slide against each other, these microscopic irregularities interlock. This creates a resistive contact force called friction, which acts in the exact opposite direction to motion.
scenes.onScreenText:
3. Frictional Resistance Vector
Friction Force (← f) opposes Velocity (v →)
scenes.subtitles: Microscopic irregularities interlock, creating an opposing friction force pointing opposite to motion.

scenes.title: Deceleration and Stopping
scenes.narration: Because the friction force opposes motion, it continuously reduces the object's speed. The crate gradually slows down until its velocity reaches zero, bringing it to a complete halt.
scenes.onScreenText:
4. Deceleration to Rest
Continuous resistance reduces speed: v → 0
scenes.subtitles: The opposing friction continuously reduces speed until the object gradually comes to a complete halt.

scenes.title: Lubrication & Rolling
scenes.narration: Applying oil or grease introduces a fluid layer that keeps solid ridges from touching, while wheels replace sliding with much smaller rolling friction. This is why farmers grease bullock cart axles!
scenes.onScreenText:
5. Reducing Friction
• Lubricants (Oil / Grease) separate ridges
• Rolling friction << Sliding friction
scenes.subtitles: Lubricants separate ridges with a fluid layer, and wheels turn heavy sliding into smooth rolling.

scenes.title: Conclusion
scenes.narration: Friction is a necessary contact force. It lets us walk and brake safely, while smart engineering helps us minimize unwanted wear and energy loss.
scenes.onScreenText:
Forces & Friction
Opposing Motion • Surface Interlocking • Village Engineering
scenes.subtitles: Friction is a necessary contact force that opposes motion and allows us to grip, walk, and brake safely.
